faqs.q: Is Google Ads Worth It for Dental Clinics?
faqs.a: Yes, if every click is tracked to a booking. Patients searching “dental implants near me” or “root canal cost” are ready to act. Google Ads fails when campaigns attract job seekers or free-camp searches, or when calls go unanswered. Negative keywords, call tracking and fast callbacks decide whether the spend returns patients.

faqs.q: How Much Should a Dental Clinic Spend on Marketing Each Month?
faqs.a: Work backwards from the patients you want, not a fixed figure. For example, 60 new patients a month at a 25% booking rate needs 240 leads. At ₹200 per lead, that’s about ₹48,000 in ad spend. Your real numbers depend on city, treatment mix and conversion rate.

faqs.q: How Long Does Dental SEO Take to Show Results?
faqs.a: Google Business Profile improvements usually show within 60 to 90 days. Organic rankings for treatment and locality searches typically move from months four to six. Returns compound from months nine to twelve, and competitive cities such as Mumbai and Bangalore can take longer.

faqs.q: Which Keywords Should a Dental Clinic Target on Google?
faqs.a: Target searches that show booking intent: “dentist near me,” “dental clinic in [locality],” “dental implants cost in [city],” “root canal treatment near me,” “clear aligners price” and “emergency dentist open now.” Avoid broad terms like “teeth” or “dental care,” which attract students and researchers rather than patients.

faqs.q: Can Dentists Advertise in India?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. India’s dental code of ethics allows dentists to advertise if they maintain decorum, but it treats false promises and paying agents to bring in patients as unethical. Websites with factual information are permitted. So clinic marketing should stay educational and accurate, without discounts or outcome guarantees.

faqs.q: Does Instagram Marketing Work for Dental Clinics?
faqs.a: It works best for treatments patients think about before booking, such as aligners, whitening and smile makeovers. Short videos of dentists explaining treatment, cost and recovery build trust. Urgent visits, like toothache appointments, come mostly from Google search and Maps rather than Instagram.

faqs.q: Can IVF Clinics Advertise Success Rates in India?
faqs.a: It’s best avoided. Success rates vary with age, diagnosis and treatment, so one headline figure can mislead patients and invite complaints under advertising standards. Sex selection must never be advertised, as Indian law prohibits it. Explaining what affects outcomes is the safer, more trusted approach.

faqs.q: Which Keywords Should IVF Clinics Target on Google?
faqs.a: Target searches that show readiness to consult: “IVF centre near me,” “IVF cost in [city],” “fertility specialist in [city],” “IUI treatment cost” and “IVF second opinion.” Broad terms like “infertility causes” bring early researchers, so use them for content, not paid ads.

faqs.q: How Much Should an IVF Centre Spend on Marketing?
faqs.a: Work backwards from consultations, not a fixed budget. Decide how many consultations each centre can handle monthly, check what share of enquiries usually book, and fund enough enquiries to fill those slots. Review cost per consultation monthly and move spend to the channels that deliver it.

faqs.q: How Long Does SEO Take to Work for a Fertility Centre?
faqs.a: Google Business Profile and page improvements usually show within 60 to 90 days. Rankings for competitive terms like “IVF centre in [city]” typically move from months four to six. Doctor-reviewed content builds trust over time, with stronger returns from months nine to twelve.

faqs.q: Should IVF Clinics Use Instagram and YouTube?
faqs.a: Yes, for education. Short videos of doctors explaining IVF steps, timelines and costs build trust during long research. Instagram and YouTube work best for awareness, not urgent bookings. Never show identifiable patients without written consent, and avoid wording that implies the viewer has a fertility problem.

faqs.q: How Can IVF Clinics Get Reviews Without Risking Patient Privacy?
faqs.a: Ask every patient for a review through a private, opt-in message after their visit, never in public. When replying, thank them without confirming any treatment or personal detail. Even a kind reply that mentions IVF can expose a patient’s private health information.

faqs.q: Can Eye Hospitals Advertise LASIK Prices?

faqs.q: Which Keywords Should Eye Centres Target on Google?

faqs.q: Does Google Ads Work for Cataract Surgery?

faqs.q: How Long Does SEO Take for an Eye Hospital?

faqs.q: Should Eye Centres Market Optical Stores and Surgery Together?
faqs.a: Keep them separate. Spectacles and lenses are lower-value, quick purchases, while surgery involves research and consultation. Combining them in one campaign lets cheaper optical clicks absorb the budget. Separate campaigns and reports show what each actually brings in.

faqs.q: How Can Eye Hospitals Reach Patients From Nearby Towns?
faqs.a: Run location-based campaigns for surrounding towns and districts, and build pages that answer travel questions: surgery duration, same-day discharge and follow-up visits. Fast WhatsApp replies and a coordinator for out-of-town patients help turn enquiries into confirmed surgery dates.

faqs.q: Is Google Ads Effective for Multi-Speciality Hospitals?
faqs.a: Yes, when campaigns are split by speciality. Patients search for “knee replacement surgery” or “cardiologist near me,” not a hospital’s name. One combined campaign lets broad departments absorb the budget. Speciality-level campaigns, call tracking and fast callbacks decide whether ad spend turns into consultations.

faqs.q: How Should a Hospital Split Its Marketing Budget Across Departments?
faqs.a: Split it by patient value and capacity, not by department size. Give more budget to specialities with high-value procedures and available OPD slots. Review the split monthly, moving spend towards departments where enquiries actually turn into consultations and admissions.

faqs.q: Can Hospitals Advertise Under NMC Rules?
faqs.a: Yes, with care. NMC rules restrict self-promotion by individual doctors, so marketing should come from the hospital, not the doctor. Content should stay educational and factual, without outcome guarantees, comparisons with other hospitals or misleading testimonials.

faqs.q: Which Hospital Departments Benefit Most From Digital Marketing?
faqs.a: Departments with planned, high-value procedures usually benefit most. These include orthopaedics, cardiology, oncology, bariatric surgery, IVF and cosmetic procedures. Patients research these options online for weeks before choosing, so search, doctor pages and follow-up have more time to influence the decision.

faqs.q: How Can Hospitals Attract Patients From Other Cities?
faqs.a: Build treatment pages that answer travel questions: cost estimates, stay duration, accommodation help and how to send reports in advance. Then reply quickly on WhatsApp and assign a coordinator. Out-of-city patients decide based on how easy the hospital makes the journey.

faqs.q: Does a Hospital Need a CRM for Patient Enquiries?
faqs.a: Yes, once enquiries come through several departments and channels. A CRM gives every enquiry a source, an owner and an outcome. Without one, calls, forms and WhatsApp messages get lost between desks, and nobody can see which campaigns lead to admissions.
